topic.title: The offsite is cheaper than a raise
topic.claim: The team offsite is a retention plan that costs less than a raise, and it works better than it should.
topic.moment: Two days at a resort, matching T-shirts, a trophy for 'Best Team Player'.

turn.believed: Offsites are a perk for good work.
turn.actually: A one-time trip costs less than a pay hike that compounds every year, and it buys loyalty for a few months.

topic.feeling: I had fun and I still feel a bit bought.
topic.villain: Budgets where one-time spend is easy and permanent salary is hard
topic.because: A raise sits in the cost base forever. A trip sits in one quarter, and the photos remind you of it for a year.
topic.payoff: The honest bit: the trip did make you stay. That's exactly why it was approved.
topic.behaviour: Companies fund offsites and team dinners while holding increments flat.
topic.mechanism: One-off spend buys goodwill without raising fixed costs.
topic.group: Employees at startups and mid-size companies
topic.send_to: The team group, right after the offsite photos go up
topic.why_now: Offsite season lines up with the months when increments get trimmed.

score.why: The offsite did make you stay, and that's why it was approved. It has an honest mixed feeling and is the one office pick, with a lived angle.
